question.text: Commodity futures contracts are standardized in terms of all the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: The identity and credit rating of the counterparty
Size and quantity of the commodity
Quality and grade of the commodity

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures contracts are standardized by quantity, quality/grade, time and place of delivery and related specifications. Buyers and sellers remain anonymous and the clearing corporation steps in as CCP, so the identity and credit rating of the counterparty is not a standardized element. The Trap: All the other items are explicitly part of contract specifications. Anonymity of counterparties, supported by CCP clearing, is a feature of the market, not a standardized contract term. Note: Standardization is what makes any contract of the same specification interchangeable, which supports liquidity in the futures market.
